semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The 'inverse dynamics model' concept is similar to inverse constrained reinforcement learning because both involve deducing internal dynamics from observed outcomes or actions. Inverse models typically look at inferring control inputs from system outputs, aligning closely with the concept of inverse constrained learning in reinforcement contexts.

parent_models.justification: Deep reinforcement learning encompasses a broad range of techniques, including those that deal with inverse dynamics and constraints. It is a higher-level category that can incorporate models focusing on inverse constrained reinforcement learning.

Reinforcement learning agents are entities designed to make decisions by learning from their environment. Simplified inverse constrained reinforcement learning could be considered a specific approach utilized by such agents.

closest_parent_model.justification: The 'reinforcement learning agent' serves as the closest parent model since it directly implements various learning strategies, including simplified inverse constrained approaches, to interact and learn effectively within environments.

child_models.justification: This model focuses on incorporating constraints within a specific reinforcement learning context (Q-learning), which is a more nuanced application similar to handling constraints in inverse settings.

closest_child_model.justification: Latent diffusion-constrained Q-learning directly deals with constraints in a reinforcement learning setting, making it closer related to simplified inverse constrained reinforcement learning due to its focus on both learning dynamics and constraints.
